messages.author: ecd92925ab6b8a4c
messages.subject: takes strangely long to run a simple model
parts:
I am completely new to stan so apologize if this has been asked before.
 
I tried my first model (code and results attached below), it is very simple, however, it takes about 60 to 70 seconds to run,. no matter I choose 1000 or 10000 iterations. It seems from the message that the actual model fitting only takes 0.077 sec (I could be wrong here), so something else must be hanging this model around.
 
I have complete information below (should be reproducible), thanks!
 
R code
 
library(rstan)
nsbj <- 100
p <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4)
dat <- cbind(n=nsbj, y=sapply(p, rbinom, n=1, size=nsbj))
prior <- c(0, 100)

  ndose <- nrow(dat)
  mu_prior <- prior[1]
  sd_prior <- prior[2]
  inputdat <- list(dat=dat, ndose=ndose, mu_prior=mu_prior, sd_prior=sd_prior)
 
  system.time(fit <- stan(file = 'try.stan', data = inputdat,
                          iter = 1000, chains = 1))
 

 
 
stan script
 
data {
  int<lower=1> ndose; // number of doses
  int dat[ndose, 2]; // data
  real mu_prior;
  real<lower=0> sd_prior;
}
parameters {
  real mu[ndose];
  real <lower=0> sd1;
  real m1;
}
transformed parameters {
  real <lower=0, upper=1> p[ndose];
  for(j in 1:ndose)
  {p[j] <- exp(mu[j]) / (1 + exp(mu[j]));}
}
model {
 
  dat[,2] ~ binomial(dat[,1], p);
  mu[1] ~ normal(m1, sd1);
  for(i in 2:ndose)
  {
    mu[i] ~ normal(mu[i-1], sd1);
    sd1 ~ inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  }
  m1 ~ normal(mu_prior, sd_prior);
}

parts:
That's because stan() has to compile the model before sampling. If you want to break up the steps, do:

myModel = stan_model("try.stan")

Then use sampling() to sample:

post = sampling(
   MyModel
   , data = inputdat 
)

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] takes strangely long to run a simple model
parts:
Hi Tony, 

Once you've run stan_model() then you can take the resulting object and pass it to sampling() as many times as you want without rerunning stan_model. So, for example, if you want to change any of the other arguments to sampling, e.g.

mod <- stan_model("foo.tan")
fit1 <- sampling(mod, data = data1, iter = 1000)
fit2 <- sampling(mod, data = data2, iter = 3000)
fit3 <- etc.

then you don't need to recompile (don't need to call stan_model). You'd only need to recompile if you changed the Stan code in "foo.stan". 

Hope that helps, 

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] takes strangely long to run a simple model
parts: Also, I just noticed a few issues in your Stan program. You have

for(i in 2:ndose)
  {
    mu[i] ~ normal(mu[i-1], sd1);
    sd1 ~ inv_gamma(0.01, 0.01);
  }

but I don't think you want sd1 inside the loop. It's just a single scalar parameter so you only need to do sd1 ~ inv_gamma(...) once. We also don't recommend those inverse-gamma priors (see section 6.2. Priors for Coefficients and Scales in the Stan manual for version 2.9 for a bit more on this topic). I think half-t distributions are in vogue these days for priors on scale parameters (more here). 

On another note, if you want you can also vectorize instead of looping by doing something like this: 

tail(mu, n-1) ~ normal(head(mu, n-1), sd1)

which is more efficient but less readable (so I would keep the loop if the model is already plenty fast and only sacrifice the clarity for speed if efficiency is an issue). Also, I would recommend using the inverse_logit function instead of computing that manually. You could also do everything on the logit scale and use binomial_logit (or bernoulli_logit depending on your data), don't require you to convert to probabilities yourself and are a bit more stable (see section 6.4 of the manual for more on this). 


Jonah
